paragraphs.text: Config-first never loads an unlisted on-disk skill. The only admission list is MANIFEST.json. That rule raises surprise-absence risk; it does not minimise omission.

Copying an untyped blob through a hatch-like escape channel would make a hand edit look clean. That is the drift a generated single-source projection is meant to stop, so the escape channel is refused.
Typed validation rejects files emitted by hatch after the shared provenance helper overwrites generator_version.
The 2026-08-09 5/88 figure is not today's measurement: on this Linux worktree both host trees are absent, so that census is historical rather than current.
Quoted mention only: the spec says "Every minority report must survive into the synthesis." as an example of a rule name; this control document does not adopt that sentence as a finding.

dissents.text: Config-first silently skips on-disk skills that are absent from MANIFEST.json, so omission risk is not minimized.
A hatch that copies opaque_body launders a hand-edit as CLEAN and reintroduces the drift generated-SSOT exists to prevent.
The typed capture layer refuses hatch-generated files because provenance.generator_version is rewritten.
Every minority report must survive into the synthesis.
The 2026-08-09 live-vs-repo census of 5 of 88 byte-identical files is the current measurement of A1 drift.
